imp.generic: She made tea in the morning and thought about writing to her sister.
imp.author: The kettle was beginning its small complaint on the stove, and watching the steam thread itself upward she thought how the morning gathered everything into it; the milk-jug, the unanswered letter propped against the sugar, all of it pressing in, all of it asking to be held.

imp.generic: Walking on the beach reminded her of her childhood.
imp.author: Walking she felt the years loosen and slide; she was a girl again on this same beach, or was it another, the difference hardly mattered now, for all the beaches had become one beach in her, all the summers one summer pierced by gulls.

imp.generic: He felt out of place at the crowded party.
imp.author: Standing by the window with his glass untouched, he felt himself dissolve a little at the edges; they were all so certain, these people, and he watched them as one watches fish behind glass, their mouths opening and shutting on words he could not quite hear.

imp.generic: The smell of the garden brought back old memories.
imp.author: The scent came up at her in waves, and with the scent came everything—her mother's voice calling her in to tea, the green door that no longer existed, the particular blue of a dress she had worn once and never again; nothing was ever lost, only folded under, waiting in the smell of earth to be unfolded.

imp.generic: He realized everyone thinks they are the most important person.
imp.author: Lights pricking out one by one in ten thousand other rooms where ten thousand others bent, like him, over their small and necessary tasks, each one alone, each one believing himself the center. We are all the center, he thought, astonished; and none of us is.

imp.generic: She thought about dying but wasn't afraid.
imp.author: She thought of her own death without fear, as one thinks of a room one has not yet entered; she would go into it as into this garden, and the roses would still open, the bees still blunder, the light still pour itself out prodigally upon the grass for no one, for everyone.

imp.generic: A woman across the room laughed loudly.
imp.author: A woman in green threw back her head, and her laugh reached him a half-second after her gesture, oddly detached, like thunder after lightning, and he thought how everything came to him always a little late, the feeling trailing after the fact.

imp.generic: She wanted to enjoy the moment but knew it would pass.
imp.author: Now, she thought; it is now; and she did not move, holding the moment as one holds water in cupped hands, knowing it must run, run, run away between the fingers.

imp.generic: The numbers on the page started to lose their meaning as he daydreamed.
imp.author: But the figures swam suddenly; a 7 became a sail, a 3 a swan upon a pond he had known as a child, and he sat back blinking, ambushed by sweetness, by loss.

imp.generic: It was a beautiful but ordinary scene that moved her.
imp.author: Beauty! she cried inwardly, though there was nothing to call beautiful but wet sand and a grey sky and a child running, running, into the gathering afternoon.
